intent.outcome: Taps.List uses one brew tap-info --json with all tap names (after brew tap), not N sequential tap-info calls. Heavy name lists stay available for detail/trust without per-tap round-trips on list.

problem.description: taps.go List: brew tap then for each name fetchTapInfo (tap-info --json one name) sequentially. Many taps = slow panel. FormulaNames/CaskNames loaded for every tap on list even if user never opens Formulae tab.

in_scope: Batch: after listing tap names, call brew tap-info --json <name...> once (or chunk if ARG_MAX risk — document chunk size if needed).
Lazy detail: if batch JSON is huge, allowed to omit FormulaNames/CaskNames on list and fetch single tap-info on Formulae/Trust detail — prefer lazy names when practical.
Update TestTapsServiceList expectations; add TestTapsBatchLoad counting runner calls.
GUI continues to work for Tap Info / Trust / Formulae tabs.

findings.description: fetchTapInfoBatch does not chunk names. With 1000+ taps the single arg list could exceed ARG_MAX (typically 128KB-2MB). Documented as out-of-scope; flag if user reports hang on huge tap counts.
findings.author: runner

findings.description: On fetchTapInfoBatch error, List caches the incomplete name-only []Tap under KeyTapsList and returns nil error. Next List within cache TTL returns incomplete data without retrying the batch — FormulaNames/CaskNames/Trust stay empty until TTL expires or InvalidateFor. Fix: do not cache on batch failure (return name-only uncached). Add TestTapsBatchFailureDoesNotPoisonCache: fail once, succeed second List, assert FormulaNames populated and tap-info called twice.
findings.author: coordinator
findings.summary: List caches name-only taps after batch failure; blocks retry

findings.description: All 12 taps are named thirdparty/tap so the test does not prove every name was passed in the batch args (a 1-name batch would still return 12 list entries from brew tap output). Use unique names (thirdparty/tap-0..N) and assert len(args)==2+N with each name present.
